label: k fed back as first or second copy-phase input
explanation: Fires in the copy phase when the input token is k at the first or second copy step (recall_idx 1 or 2), meaning k was original token 0 or 1. Magnitude: strong (about 0.85-1.0 of max) when k is the first copied token (step right after <DEL>, first_tok == k), which carries about 82% of the mass; weak (about 0.05-0.3) when k is the second copied token. Never fires on k at later copy steps, on k during the original phase (only tiny traces), on the delimiter, or on any other token. Most false positives are k at recall_idx 2 in short sequences (L = 3-4) where the feature stays off.

issues: The only systematic false-positive class is k at recall_idx 2 in short sequences, which the explanation already admits. On the test split: at L==3 the predicate is never right (0 of 444 predicted steps are active); at L==4 precision is 0.54 (2477 predicted); at L>=5 precision is 0.9999. The label 'first or second copy-phase input' overclaims a little, because the second-input case only holds reliably for L>=4, and cleanly for L>=5.

The half-on, half-off behaviour at L==4, recall_idx 2 did not split cleanly on orig(0/2/3) being a digit or a vowel, or on n_digits (precision 0.41-0.60 in every case). It looks like weak activations sitting near the firing threshold, not a hidden variable.

Magnitude claims hold up. recall_idx 1 holds 81.8% of activation mass in dev (0.813 mass recall in test), with examples around 0.85-0.94 of max. recall_idx 2 holds about 18% of mass, with examples around 0.2-0.36 of max, slightly above the stated 0.05-0.3. The original phase has 49 tiny activations (e.g. k at orig_idx 4 at about 0.02-0.05 of max), recall_idx 3 has 5, the delimiter has 0 and other tokens have 0.
Excluding L==3 alone (recall_idx 2 & L>=4) raises test precision to 0.966 and F1 to 0.982, with mass recall unchanged (0.9999). This is a small but principled refinement.
